info.bio:
Hay 3 bandas con el nombre X

Banda punk proveniente de Los Angeles, formada en 1977. Sus integrantes son John Doe, Billy Zoom, Exene Cervenka y DJ Bonebrake .

Banda australiana, también de punk y al igual que la americana, formada en 1977 y liderada por Ian Rilen. 

Un grupo japonés de Speed, Thrash, Power Metal con algunos tintes de progresivo formada en 1982 y que, tras 10 años, pasó a denominarse  X Japan En verano de 1978 Yoshiki Hayashi

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.
scenes.family: Punk, new wave, hardcore y noise

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

podcast.title: Marriage and Divorce (1980-1985)
podcast.body: Xine Servenka (singer) and John Doe (guitarist) of the San Francisco punk band X were married from 1980 to 1985. "Singer Xine Servenka and guitarist John Doe were married from 1980 to 1985."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Adding Vindication to West Coast Scene
podcast.body: X was a crucial band that brought much-needed validation to the burgeoning West Coast punk scene. Their distinct sound and lyrical approach earned them significant influence. "Then came X, the group that added some much needed vindication to the West Coast scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Groundbreaking Punk Band
podcast.body: X is recognized as a groundbreaking San Francisco punk band. "X, the groundbreaking San Francisco punk band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lasting Influence in California
podcast.body: X's innovative blend of punk and lyrical depth had an important and lasting influence on the newly developing music scene in California, shaping the direction for future bands. "This would have an important and lasting influence in the newly born scene in California."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent L.A. Punk Band
podcast.body: X was one of the notable bands that frequently played at The Masque, a club on Hollywood Boulevard crucial to the development of Southern California punk. "This was the home to places like X, the Germans, the blasters, the dills, the screamers, the weirdos, the zeros."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Punk Sound with Intelligent Lyrics
podcast.body: The band's music was characterized by a strong punk sound, but it was elevated by smart and intelligent lyrics. This combination provided a deeper, more thoughtful dimension to the raw energy of punk rock. "They sounded very punk, but they laced their stuff with smart and intelligent lyrics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sea Snail Species
podcast.body: A type of sea snail found in the Pacific off Easter Island is known as *Dispressizona Xorum*, named after the punk band The X from the Netherlands. The band expressed their excitement about this honor, even featuring the snail on their 2003 album "Turn." "The type of sea snail found in the Pacific off Easter Island is known as Dispressizona Xorum after a punk band from the Netherlands called the X."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shared Stages with The Go-Go's
podcast.body: X shared stages with The Go-Go's during the late 1970s in the vibrant Los Angeles punk scene. "They shared stages with groups like X in the germs."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Subsequent Marriages and Divorces (Xine Servenka)
podcast.body: After divorcing John Doe, Xine Servenka later married actor Vigo Morgan Stern. This marriage also ended in divorce, and she subsequently married and divorced again. "She later married actor Vigo Morgan Stern. That ended in divorce before she got married and divorced again."

xref.title: "The X Files" Movie Soundtrack Spoken Word
xref.body: Chris Carter, the creator of "The X Files," contributed a strange spoken word piece to the soundtrack of "The X Files" movie. This hidden track, found at the very end of the album, discusses a syndicate's secret vaccine against "black oil," the breakdown of their code of honor, and threats from within and without, mentioning agents Mulder and Scully. "It's a spoken word piece by Sirius Creator Chris Carter, and it's just too weird not to play here."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Coldplay's "Talk" Melody Source
xref.body: Coldplay intentionally borrowed the melody line for their song "Talk" from the *X&Y* album from Kraftwerk's "Computer Love," and Kraftwerk was agreeable to this. "And yes, Coldplay does know they left the melody line for Talk from the X and Y album. In fact, they did that on purpose, and Kraftwerk was cool with it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cultural Impact and Name Origin
xref.body: Even non-musicians were captivated by The Pixies' influence; Chris Carter, the creator of The X-Files, named the lead character in his series Millennium, Frank Black, after the name Black Francis adopted after the Pixies disbanded. "Chris Carter, the creator of the X-Files, named the lead character in the series Millennium, Frank Black, because that was the name Black Francis assumed after the Pixies broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

xref.title: Dave Grohl Leg Break Faked Theory
xref.body: Despite Dave Grohl breaking his leg in Guttenberg, Sweden in June 2015 and finishing the show, some people claim the injury was faked. They argue that everything, from the canceled shows to the publicly available X-rays, was a ruse to allow the band to return triumphantly with Grohl's famous throne and sell commemorative t-shirts, even though the tour, including a Wembley Stadium show, was already sold out. "They claim that this was all faked. Everything from the canceled shows to the X-rays that were made available to the public."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Discovery and Signing with MCA
xref.body: The Headstones were discovered by Cam Carpenter and Tony Wanamaker, who secured them a showcase at the X-ray and Ultra Sound Club. A pivotal moment was the unexpected appearance and endorsement of Gord Downie and Paul Langlois from The Tragically Hip (who were also signed to MCA), which swayed MCA to sign the Headstones despite initial concerns about their "dangerous" image. "I remember when MCA and Cam Carpenter, you know, signed us at ultrasound, they were like, yeah, is it they're a little dangerous yet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Headstones: In Their Own Words Part 1

xref.title: Instrumental in The Headstones' Signing
xref.body: Gord Downie and Paul Langlois, who were signed with MCA at the time, provided crucial support for The Headstones. Their unexpected appearance and endorsement at The Headstones' showcase at the X-ray and Ultra Sound Club in Toronto were instrumental in convincing MCA Records to sign the band. "The backing of Gordownee and Paul Langwau who were with MC at the time showing up at our, guesswork show at our gas work show. And also the ultrasound show, the showcase... That had just as much to do with us getting signed as our, you know, incredible talent."

xref.title: Three Singers Post-Weiland – Chester Bennington Moonlighted from Linkin Park; Jeff Gutt Won Online Audition
xref.body: Scott Weiland was fired and rehired multiple times; the first replacement attempt involved David Coutts in a short-lived side project called Talk Show that failed entirely. Weiland was fired for good in 2013; he died of a drug overdose in 2016 without reconciling with the band. Chester Bennington of Linkin Park — a lifelong STP fan — was brought in for approximately two and a half years, was made an official member, toured, and recorded two tracks before returning to Linkin Park. His replacement was Jeff Gutt, found through an online audition that also briefly considered John Borja from the Philippines; Gutt had been a runner-up on Season 3 of *The X Factor* and was confirmed by fall 2017. "Chester was also a lifelong STP fan since, well, since he could remember."
